newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil price recovers after U.S. cold snap.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil price recovers after U.S. cold snap.

text.p: Venezuela's basket price of crude oil and oil products rose by nearly 50 cents per barrel over the past week to close at $16.23 per barrel on Friday, the Ministry of Energy and Mines said.
The rise was a rare piece of good news for oil exporters who have seen prices plummet by over 20 percent since the beginning of the year.
Traders in New York attributed last week's recovery to a recent cold snap in the United States and production problems in Nigeria.
So far in April, the Venezuela's average basket price stood at $15.98 per barrel, versus $17.00 in March, $18.70 in February and $20.36 in January.

For the year-to-date, the price was $18.15 per barrel on Friday, against $18.28 a week before. The basket closed 1996 with one of the highest average prices for several years at $18.39 per barrel, against $14.84 for 1995.

Venezuela's government has based its 1997 budget on an average price for the year of $14.00 per barrel, although Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta has said he expects it to average higher than $15.50.
